items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Cecil Taylor is mentioned by the interviewer as an example of an American artist grounded in tradition, but Slide Hampton does not mention Cecil Taylor in his response, nor does he describe any personal interaction or relationship with him.

ctx.x: I think that’s some of the freshest music that I’m hearing that I see connected with tradition. You were talking about free music, I think, when I was out of the room. You were talking about how it didn’t seem to be grounded in anything, or seemed to have sort of cast aside . . . Kimery: No, actually, we were talking about a comparison between the European artists and the American artists, where the American artists . . .
That’s precisely what I’m talking about Kimery: They’re grounded in the tradition of the music.
